subject: Control plane & network criteria: validation plan and competitive summary
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Morris <claire.morris@bankcorp.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 7 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Control plane & network criteria: validation plan and competitive summary

Hi Claire — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap while it's fresh and a proposed validation plan so your SREs can pick the first tests.

Call recap (short):
- Primary asks from your side: no egress of customer data, customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS), control-plane isolation (VPC or on-prem), and a clear network validation checklist for air-gapped feasibility.
- You also asked for a short competitive note comparing Redwood to hyperscaler-managed inference endpoints and a list of the next tests your SREs should run.

Where Redwood starts differentiated (very short bullets):
- Private control plane option: we can deploy a customer-facing control plane inside your VPC (private IPs only) or as an on-prem control plane package with no external egress.
- Runtime isolation: model execution happens in your dedicated GPU pool—no shared tenant compute.
- KMS/HSM integration: support for cloud KMS (BYOK) or HSM-backed keys for crypto operations.
- Networking flexibility: supports VPC peering, transit gateway attachment, and for air-gapped pilots we offer an appliance-based bootstrap and certificate pinning model.

Proposed validation plan (first tranche):
1) Network reachability check: your SREs run a traceroute and HTTP health probe to the proposed control-plane endpoint (we'll provide an internal IP/host).
2) Egress proof: we run a packet capture during a short API test to show no customer payload leaves your VPC (we'll coordinate a live session).
3) KMS proof: crypto handshake demonstrating we can use your CMK/HSM for model decryption/signing.
4) Latency baseline: 30-minute steady state at 25–50 rps against a dedicated capacity node to show tail-latency and median numbers.

Attachments: redwood-private-brief.pdf (architecture + options), SOC2-summary.pdf (audit excerpts), network-validation-checklist.xlsx (initial test list).

Ask: can you confirm the top 3 acceptance criteria you want us to prioritize, and two possible 60–90 minute slots next week for the network validation? Once you confirm we will assign owners and send an infra-ready checklist to your SRE team.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Redwood Inference — Production-first inference runtime and private deployment options
From: Claire Morris <claire.morris@bankcorp.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 7 Nov 2027 12:05:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Control plane & network criteria: validation plan and competitive summary

Kimberly — thanks for the clear recap. Helpful. Top-level acceptance criteria from our side (in priority):
1) Absolute no egress of decrypted customer data to the public internet or third-party control planes (we need strong evidence).
2) Support for HSM-backed key usage and auditable key control flows.
3) Ability to run a control plane inside our VPC (no external control-plane DNS lookups) or a local on-prem control plane if the VPC option doesn't meet our firewall policies.

Additional asks:
- Can you provide a one-page comparison vs major hyperscalers (Azure/AWS) that highlights control plane egress, key control, and on-prem options? That will help legal and our platform risk team.
- For the latency baseline: we want realistic tail numbers at 512 tokens and at 1k tokens for both cold and warm-cache.
- Can you share the exact URLs/IPs and a minimal command list for the traceroute/health check so we can run it in our staging VPC?

Availability: we can do Mon 2027-11-08 10:00–11:30 EST or Tue 2027-11-09 14:00–15:30 EST. Please pick and send us the checklist we should follow.

Thanks — Claire
Claire Morris
Head of Platform Security, BankCorp Financial
claire.morris@bankcorp.com
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Morris <claire.morris@bankcorp.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 8 Nov 2027 08:37:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Control plane & network criteria: validation plan and competitive summary

Claire / Kim — I'm looping in Marcus and Ben to own the infra and pricing items. Quick mapping of Claire's asks to our capabilities and proposed owners/timeline: 

Mapping: 
- No egress of decrypted data: Redwood offers both (a) a private control plane deployed inside customer VPC (private IP, no public DNS) and (b) an on-prem control plane appliance for fully air-gapped setups. Owner: Marcus Lin (Infra).
- HSM/CMK integration: we support both cloud KMS BYOK and HSM workflows (FIPS-validated chains). Owner: Ben Carter (Security & Integration).
- Control-plane choices & proof: we will prepare two artifacts — a one-page hyperscaler comparison and a minimal on-prem architecture diagram. Owner: Kimberly (SE) + Marcus.

Proposed validation tests (owners + timing):
1) Traceroute & HTTP probe (action: we provide target IP/hostname + exact curl/traceroute commands) — Owner: Marcus — run Mon 11/08 10:00 EST (you confirmed availability).
2) Egress verification session (live packet capture with your SRE + our infra engineer) — Owner: Marcus — follow-up same day if traceroute green.
3) KMS handshake demo (we'll bring sample CMK and show key-wrap/key-unwrap) — Owner: Ben — schedule Tue 11/09 14:00 EST if you want a separate slot.
4) Latency baseline: we will schedule a 30-minute dedicated-capacity run during the week after the network tests to capture cold/warm cache stats at 512/1k tokens — Owner: Kimberly — we'll share data format and metrics to capture.

Next steps (immediate):
- Kimberly: provide the minimal commands and the target IP/host for the traceroute by EOD today.
- Claire: confirm whether you want the KMS session on Tue 11/09 at 14:00 or combined with the traceroute day.
- Ben/Marcus: prepare the one-page comparison vs hyperscalers and the internal lab checklist.

We will also include an engineering contact for live packet capture (Marcus).

Thanks — looking forward to running this.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 8 Nov 2027 16:45:00 -05:00
Subject: Fwd: Control plane & network criteria: validation plan and competitive summary

Kim / Steph — quick add for the internal playbook and positioning vs hyperscalers:
- Hyperscalers typically require a control plane outside the customer's VPC (or rely on vendor endpoints that have to call back to managed services). That often means outbound IPs or VPC endpoints that still result in egress from the customer's control.
- Redwood's two-prong offering (in-VPC control plane OR on-prem appliance) lets us claim a clean separation: zero-control-plane-egress in the on-prem case, and private-only control-plane traffic in the in-VPC case.

Action items for us internally:
1) Produce the one-pager comparison (security, egress behavior, KMS story, deployment models) — owner: Ben Carter — deliver by Tue 11/09 EOD.
2) Finalize the traceroute/health-check payload and provide the sample PCAP template we'll use in the egress proof session — owner: Marcus Lin — deliver by Mon 11/08 09:30 EST so Claire's team can run the check.
3) Prep the latency-run instance reservation details and cost estimate for the dedicated 30-minute baseline run — owner: Kimberly Park — provide by Wed 11/10.

I'll draft the comparison now and attach to the hubspot deal once ready.

-ben
Ben Carter
VP, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
